Based on the search results, here's what I found about SimpleVLA-RL:

## Overview

SimpleVLA-RL is an efficient RL framework tailored for VLA models that builds upon veRL and introduces VLA-specific trajectory sampling, scalable parallelization, multi-environment rendering, and optimized loss computation.

## Key Motivation

Vision-Language-Action models face challenges including the scarcity and high cost of large-scale robotic trajectories required for SFT scaling and limited generalization to tasks under distribution shift, which SimpleVLA-RL addresses through reinforcement learning to scale VLA training beyond limited datasets.

## Performance Results

When applied to OpenVLA-OFT, SimpleVLA-RL achieves 99% of state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO and an 80% relative improvement on RoboTwin 1.0 & 2.0, outperforming π₀ with proposed exploration-enhancing strategies. Additionally, it achieved a 120% relative improvement on real robots, outperforming RDT.

## Novel Findings

A novel phenomenon called "pushcut" was identified during RL training, wherein the policy discovers unseen patterns beyond those seen in previous training process.

## Publication Status

SimpleVLA-RL was accepted to ICLR 2026.

I found several highly relevant papers on arxiv.org related to token-level priority in supervised fine-tuning (SFT) from 2026. Here are the main results:

## Primary Result

The most directly relevant paper is "Supervised Fine-Tuning Needs to Unlock the Potential of Token Priority," which advocates Token Priority as the essential bridge, formalizing Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) not as simple optimization but as a precise distribution reshaping process that aligns raw data with the ideal alignment manifold.

This paper (arxiv 2602.01227, published February 2026) explores several key concepts:

- Token Priority allows filtering noise in SFT by identifying and masking easy, surface-level patterns to prevent the model from overfitting to the static training distribution, forcing it to focus on the "long-tail" logic tokens that dictate generalization.

- The fundamental premise of Token Priority is that optimization can be performed at the atomic token level.

## Related Papers

Other relevant 2026 papers on token-level SFT include:

1. **ProFit** (arxiv 2601.09195): ProFit selectively masks low-probability tokens to prevent surface-level overfitting.

2. **Segment-Level Attribution** (arxiv 2602.00425): Token-level methods typically utilize token logits and entropy to prioritize salient tokens but ignore semantic coherence.

3. **TLPO** (arxiv 2604.26553): Token-Level Policy Optimization addresses how sequence-level objectives lack the granularity to penalize specific error-inducing tokens without suppressing the valid surrounding context.

content.text:
Here are the most relevant recent competing works for your paper on adaptively prioritizing VLA training data via intra-action-chunk temporal loss profiles:

---

**Most directly competing:** [Supervised Fine-Tuning Needs to Unlock the Potential of Token Priority](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01227) (Feb 2026) formalizes SFT as distribution reshaping at the token level, masking easy/surface-level tokens to force learning on "long-tail" logic tokens. This is the closest conceptual competitor -- though it targets LLMs, not VLA action chunks. Related: [ProFit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09195) (Jan 2026) does probability-guided token selection during SFT, and [TLPO](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.26553) (Apr 2026) introduces token-level policy optimization. [Segment-Level Attribution](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.00425) (ICLR 2026) critiques pure token-level methods for ignoring semantic coherence -- a point your temporal-profile approach may naturally address.

**VLA fine-tuning landscape:** [SimpleVLA-RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09674) (ICLR 2026) scales VLA training via RL rather than smarter SFT, achieving 99% SOTA on LIBERO and 80% improvement on RoboTwin. [VLA-GSE](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06175v1) (May 2026) proposes generalized/specialized expert mixtures for parameter-efficient VLA fine-tuning. [ConRFT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05450) and [pi_RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25889) explore RL fine-tuning of VLAs. These are complementary (RL vs. SFT data prioritization) rather than directly competing.

**Benchmarks:** Pi0.5 and RoboMimic/LIBERO remain the dominant evaluation targets. No new benchmark specifically targeting data-efficiency or temporal loss analysis was found.

**Key gap your work fills:** None of the token-priority SFT papers (Token Priority, ProFit, TLPO) operate in the VLA/action-chunk domain, and none exploit the temporal structure within action chunks. The VLA fine-tuning papers focus on RL or architecture rather than data-level prioritization during SFT. Your intra-action-chunk temporal loss approach appears to occupy a distinct and unclaimed niche.
